title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from Lebanon
official_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from Lebanon.
likelihoodReason: Failed in the House on June 4, 2026 by a 92-324 vote. As a concurrent resolution it carries no force of law and is not presented to the President; the House defeat ends its progress.
summary: Directs the President to withdraw U.S. military forces from Lebanon within 7 days, using Congress's war powers authority.
brief: Directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon no later than 7 days after the resolution is adopted.

top_lines.headline: Withdrawal of Forces from Lebanon
subs: Directs removal of U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon
Deadline: 7 days after the resolution is adopted
Invokes section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution

sections.label: Section 1 — Removal of United States Armed Forces from Lebanon

items.main: Directs the President to remove all U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon no later than 7 days after the resolution is adopted.
items.detail: Acts under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1544(c)), which allows Congress to direct the removal of armed forces by concurrent resolution. The resolution sets the removal deadline at not later than 7 days after its adoption.

gaps: The resolution directs withdrawal from Lebanon but does not define which forces, units, or deployments it covers.
It sets a 7-day removal deadline but specifies no consequence or enforcement mechanism if forces are not withdrawn.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Miller
featured_quotes.text: Like most of my colleagues, whether they will admit it or not, I am a little confused. The United States, to my knowledge, doesn't have any troops in Lebanon. In fact, the last time American servicemembers were deployed in Lebanon was in 1984. Even though the gentlewoman from Michigan believes that the U.S. is the root of all evil, the United States is playing a vital role in advancing peace, security, and stability in Lebanon as we currently speak.
